identity.title: Physical properties of dusty protoplanetary disks in Lupus: evidence for viscous evolution?

paper_type_evidence.quote: In this paper we analyze a sub-sample of the ALMA Cycle 2 continuum observations at 890 $\mu$m of the Lupus disks presented by (cite: Ansdell:2016qf) (id: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2013.1.00220.S).

question.value: What are the dust surface density profiles, sizes and masses of Lupus disks from uv-plane fits of ALMA 890 um continuum, and does the mass-size relation differ from Taurus/Ophiuchus (viscous evolution)?

evidence.quote: By modeling the continuum emission with a physical disk model for passively irradiated disks (cite: Chiang:2010fk; 2001ApJ...560..957D) we determine the surface density profile of more than 20 disks and we put constraints on their midplane temperature.
(id: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2013.1.00220.S)

method.value: Exclude edge-on, gapped, binary, no-stellar-parameter, irregular and unresolved (F<4 mJy) disks from 61 detections, add IM Lup

evidence.quote: This results in a sub-sample of 35 sources.

method.value: Compare observed Herschel/J-band spectral slopes with model slopes for varying flaring factor f; adopt single f for all disks

evidence.quote: we find that a disk flaring reduced by a factor $\approx3$ ($f=0.3$) gives a good representation of the slopes at all the three bands simultaneously.
We adopt this value for all the fits that we perform in this study.

validation.value: Fits repeated for f = 0.1, 0.3, 1.0: temperature changes up to factor 1.5, Rc by at most 10%

evidence.quote: the surface density profile remains mostly unaltered with the cut-off radius $R_c$ varying by 10% at most.

analysis_steps.goal: Fit visibilities with two-layer disk model

method.value: Synthetic image Fourier-transformed and sampled at observed uv points; chi^2 on visibilities; MCMC with 7 free parameters

evidence.quote: for a given set of values of the free parameters the model produces a synthetic image of the disk that is then Fourier-transformed and sampled in the same $(u,v)-$locations of the observed visibilities.

key_parameters.value: R0 = 10 au fixed; gamma in [-2,2], Sigma0 0.05-400 g/cm2, Rc 2-400 au, i 0-90, PA 0-180, offsets +/-2"

evidence.quote: | ${R_{\mathrm{c}}}$ |        2 au        |      400 au       |
we perform the fits using one hundred chains

assumptions.value: dust-to-gas ratio 0.01; midplane amax=1.023 cm, q=3.0; kappa890=3.37 cm2/g; minimum temperature 7 K

evidence.quote: assumed to be constant and equal to the typical ISM value $\zeta=0.01$
7 K, which is the minimum temperature allowed in the model

fitting.value: Affine-invariant ensemble MCMC (emcee); posterior exp(-chi2/2) with uniform priors within bounds; median and 16-84% interval

evidence.quote: The posterior PDF is computed as $\exp(-\chi^{2}/2)$ within a rectangular domain in the parameter space

validation.value: Deprojected visibility comparison and CLEAN residual maps; normalized chi-square 1.0+/-0.2

evidence.quote: the best-fit model has usually a normalized chi-square of $1.0\pm0.2$

method.value: Rout = radius containing 95% of model flux; Mdust by integrating dust surface density from 0.1 au to Rout

evidence.quote: $R_{\mathrm{in}}=0.1\,\textrm{au}$ is the inner edge of the radial grid of the model (fixed for all the disks).

validation.value: Compared with Ansdell et al. masses (T=20 K): within factor 2 for most

evidence.quote: accurate within a factor of 2 at a 1$\sigma$ level for the majority of disks (15 out of 20).

method.value: Bayesian linear regression (linmix) of log F890 vs log Rc for Taurus/Oph, Lupus and combined; Anderson-Darling test on perpendicular offsets

evidence.quote: we perform a linear regression using the Bayesian algorithm by (cite: Kelly:2007lq)

key_parameters.value: uniform priors on coefficients; fluxes normalized to 150 pc; Taurus 1.3 mm extrapolated with alpha=3.0

evidence.quote: using an average spectral index $\alpha=3.0$ that corresponds to moderate grain growth

fitting.value: linmix Bayesian regression with errors on both axes

evidence.quote: we perform a linear regression using the Bayesian algorithm by (cite: Kelly:2007lq) which allows the uncertainties on both axes to be included in the computation.
we use the implementation of the MCMC algorithm provided by the Python package `emcee`
using the software CASA 4.5.0
We use the `linmix` Python package which implements (cite: Kelly:2007lq)

Figures have been generated using the Python-based `matplotlib` package
Staircase plots of PDFs have been generated with a user-modified version of the Python-based `triangle` package
The average radial slope for the sample of 22 disks is $<\gamma> = 0\pm 0.6$
The AD test on the full sample gives a very low probability that the two samples are drawn by the same parent distribution ($\le 0.2$%).
then the null hypothesis cannot be excluded (p$\sim$8%)

findings_qualitative.value: Most disks are well described by a smooth exponentially tapered profile; IM Lup and Sz 98 show ring-like residuals

evidence.quote: except for Sz 98 and IM Lup, for which we find a ring-like residual emission with flux $\lesssim 15\%$ of the integrated flux.

findings_qualitative.value: Masses are systematically larger than constant-20 K estimates because model disk-averaged temperatures are below 20 K

evidence.quote: Our masses tend to be slightly larger as our disk-averaged temperatures $<T_\mathrm{mid}>$ are generally smaller than 20 K.

claims.hypothesis: Do Lupus disks differ in mass-size relation from younger Taurus/Ophiuchus disks?
claims.experiment: Linmix regressions and Anderson-Darling test on offsets
claims.result: Lupus relation lies below Taurus/Oph; AD p<=0.2% for full sample, ~8% for 0.7-1 Msun
claims.finding: Lupus disks larger and fainter, tentatively consistent with viscous spreading; other mechanisms not excluded

evidence.quote: We observe that the Lupus disks appear generally larger and fainter (less massive) than those in Taurus-Auriga/Ophiuchus.

claims.hypothesis: Are constant 20 K flux-to-mass conversions biased?
claims.experiment: Compare fitted masses with Ansdell et al.
claims.result: Masses within factor 2, slightly larger; no Tmid trend with stellar properties
claims.finding: Constant-T assumption introduces no bias vs stellar mass

evidence.quote: We observed no trend between $T_\mathrm{mid}$ and the stellar mass and luminosity.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Radial drift, photoevaporation, grain growth, planet formation as alternatives to viscous spreading cannot be ruled out

evidence.quote: The current observations at 890$\mu$m do not allow us to rule out these alternative processes.

limitations_admitted.value: Constant dust-to-gas ratio and constant opacity assumed; slope may be shallower than real

evidence.quote: we caution that the slope of $\Sigma(R)$ derived here might be shallower than the real one

referee_caveats_inferred: Single average flaring factor applied to all disks
Taurus/Oph comparison sample is biased to high masses and heterogeneous
Lupus III distance 200 pc vs Gaia 150 pc affects the offset
